pattern: Option '(.+?)' in section '(.+?)' must be specified
title: Required option missing
fix: Add `{0}:` to the [{1}] section of printer.cfg. The Klipper Config Reference lists the expected value.

pattern: Section '(.+?)' is not a valid config section
title: Unknown config section
fix: [{0}] isn't a section Klipper recognises. Check for a typo, a missing prefix (like `stepper_z` or `gcode_macro NAME`), or a feature your Klipper version lacks.

pattern: Option '(.+?)' is not valid in section '(.+?)'
title: Option not allowed here
fix: Remove or rename `{0}` in [{1}]. It is misspelled or belongs to a different section.

pattern: Unable to parse option '(.+?)' in section '(.+?)'
title: Bad value format
fix: The value of `{0}` in [{1}] isn't in the expected format (number, pin name, or comma list). Compare it with the Config Reference.

title: Unknown pin prefix
fix: The pin prefix `{0}` matches no configured chip. Check the pin spelling and that the matching [mcu {0}] or expander section exists.

title: Unknown G-code command
fix: `{0}` isn't defined. Check for a typo, add a [gcode_macro {0}] section, or confirm the module that provides it is enabled.

title: Axis not homed
fix: Run G28 before moves, or add it near the start of your PRINT_START macro.

title: Move outside printer limits
fix: Check position_min/position_max on each stepper and that your macro isn't moving past them. Home first.

pattern: Heater (\S+) not heating at expected rate
title: Heater not heating
fix: Check heater wiring, thermistor seating (a loose sensor trips this), and the heater pin. Re-run PID tuning afterward. Don't leave the printer unattended until it's resolved.

title: Thermistor reading invalid
fix: Usually a disconnected or shorted thermistor, or a wrong sensor_pin or sensor_type. Check wiring and pin before restarting.

title: MCU connection problem
fix: Check the USB/serial cable and power, then confirm the `serial:` path in [mcu] matches `ls /dev/serial/by-id/`. Run FIRMWARE_RESTART afterward.

pattern: Timer too close|Rescheduled timer in the past
title: MCU timing error
fix: Often a flaky USB cable, electrical noise, or an overloaded host. Try another cable and check Pi power and CPU load.

title: Macro template error
fix: Klipper couldn't render `{0}`. Look for an undefined variable, an unclosed brace or `{% %}` block, or a wrong `printer.` object name in that macro.

pattern: No trigger on (\S+) after full movement
title: Endstop never triggered
fix: Check the {0} endstop or probe wiring, its pin and pull-up/invert markers (`^`, `!`), and test with QUERY_ENDSTOPS.

title: Probe already triggered
fix: The probe reads triggered at rest. Check pin inversion (`!`), wiring, and that nothing touches it. QUERY_PROBE shows the live state.

title: Endstop stuck triggered
fix: Check pin inversion (`!`), wiring, and that the axis really moved off the switch. QUERY_ENDSTOPS shows the live state.

title: Extrusion too large for one move
fix: Check slicer line width and flow, and the extruder `rotation_distance`. Raise `max_extrude_cross_section` in [extruder] only if the move is intended.

title: Nozzle too cold to extrude
fix: Heat the nozzle above `min_extrude_temp` before extruding. In macros, wait with M109 before any extrusion.

title: Unknown heater name
fix: `{0}` isn't a configured heater. Check the spelling and that the matching [heater_generic] or [extruder] section exists.

title: TMC driver not responding
fix: Check driver wiring and power, the uart/spi pin settings, and that the driver is seated. A wrong `uart_address` is a common cause.

pattern: pin '(.+?)' is not a valid pin name on mcu '(.+?)'
title: Invalid pin name
fix: `{0}` isn't a valid pin on mcu `{1}`. Check your board's pinout and the spelling, including any prefix such as `^` or `!`.

pattern: pin (\S+) used multiple times in config
title: Pin used twice
fix: Two sections claim pin {0}. Find the duplicate in printer.cfg and give each function its own pin.

pattern: Printer is not ready|Printer is shutdown
title: Printer needs a restart
fix: Fix the error above, then run FIRMWARE_RESTART (or RESTART for config-only changes).
